disclosures: Registration: the question, priors, case inputs, benchmarks, seed, draw counts and the 15 sensitivity rows were fixed in a plan before any model code existed (sha256 02aba2506065add1189d8a6a695209f0ce4dd47e2273ef8c4effbadb82912b2b, recorded on the wiki page reference:bdbv-nigeria-forecast-precommitment-2026-10-20 at 2026-10-20T22:50:33Z). The plan is internal; its rules are restated in the inputs. No parameter was changed after seeing model output.

Gaps in the plan were filled before the first run, each by a rule written down first: (1) Kenya 2026's e_hosp 0.4 to 1.0, pre_level STANDARD and e_fun 1.0, from the 9 October forecast's own inputs by the same hull rule the plan uses for f_pre; (2) the funeral term, which has no registered pathway, is its own row, with death if any on days 14 to 24; (3) onward infection 2 to 8 days after the parent's onset, the Kenya escape module's shift, for the plan's time to the infectiousness peak; (4) an onward case takes its parent's listing status; (5) offspring of each case are negative binomial with the draw's k; (6) Ebola-grade precautions start uniformly on days 12 to 14, with care before them weighted toward their start at the Kenya growth rates and care after them spread over 3 to 10 days; (7) community exposure is uniform from onset to day 4; (8) the unlisted share applies to every first-generation case; (9) later importations arrive from day 13 (20 October); (10) the incubation rows keep shape 3; (11) B2 uses the lower bound of the coded f_pre range; (12) the listing-day row moves only the detection rule.
The plan writes R2 = rho * R_comm * E2 * P2 without the misfit factor theta. It is implemented as written, so the calibrated theta shapes the first generation only.

Evidence added after registration, with no input changed: WHO's Regional Office for Africa states that a laboratory test confirmed Bundibugyo virus on 20 October and that symptoms began four days after arrival in Nigeria, which agrees with the plan's travel-before-onset inputs; Uganda's Ministry of Health states, as preliminary information, that the traveller had been in the eastern DRC and transited Uganda without symptoms, and that the location of exposure is under investigation. WHO's species statement effectively settles the void condition about a different ebolavirus species; the void rule is kept as registered.
No authority has said where the first case was infected, and nothing here assumes it. Nothing here identifies a person or a facility.

The 13 frozen episodes were coded after their outcomes were known, and Kenya 2026 was added knowing its outcome, although its features are the 9 October forecast's inputs, fixed before any secondary case was reported. The validation is over the same episodes that inform the calibration, so its scores are optimistic.

The setting reproduction numbers are Zaire ebolavirus values from Conakry in 2014, inherited from the 9 October model with its misfit factor and transmissibility scale; no Bundibugyo setting-specific estimate exists.
The 80 percent interval covers parameter and scenario uncertainty inside this model, with the incubation period fixed. It does not cover model-structure error and is not a worst case.

Count tiers, the decomposition by pathway and the pathway shares come from a forward simulation of the same weighted draws on a separate random stream; its probability of YES is reported beside the closed-form headline as a check. The onward-case part of the closed form is computed on grids (parent onset every 0.25 days, 33 nodes in the reported fraction of a parent's offspring) with linear interpolation, an error far below the Monte Carlo error.
Third-generation cases are not modelled: one needs a second-generation case first, which would itself resolve the question in nearly every timing.
The later-importation term (P6) is judgement, small, and reported separately.

Correction after the first run, before any number was shown to anyone: the conditioning note printed the change from the unconditioned value with the wrong sign. The text was corrected; no number, input or parameter changed. The first run's payload sha256, 2f2fced947373a6432e3b0632b26447a4687a376e798670f23450783af1a6e4a, is recorded on the wiki precommitment page beside this version's.
This forecast is additive. Block 11 and every Kenya forecast stay frozen and are scored as registered, and this is not a calibration row unless the founder rules otherwise.

Without conditioning, the probability of a qualifying case is 0.374; given no further case reported by the end of 20 October it is 0.326, a change of -0.047 (12.7 percent of the unconditioned value), so the registration-day conditioning carries more information than the registered plan expected: under the registered detection rule, listed contacts with onset before day 13 are confirmed from day 13, and part of that mass would already have been reported by the end of 20 October. No qualifying report can exist before the window opens on 21 October, so the conditioning is on no report of a further case that would otherwise qualify, as in the Kenya forecasts.

Benchmark B2 rests on 2 episodes (lbr-2014-03-lofa, uga-2026-05-kampala), 2 of them among the three episodes whose YES the Kenya module marks contestable. It is a reference rate, not a forecast for Nigeria.
The forward simulation gives 0.326 for the headline quantity against the closed form's 0.326.

question: Will Nigeria report at least one further laboratory-confirmed case of this outbreak, beyond the first case confirmed on 2026-10-20, that is not a new importation, with confirmation dated 2026-10-21 to 2026-11-17 and first reported by an authority by 2026-11-20?

registration.note: The question, priors, case inputs, benchmarks, seeds and sensitivity rows were fixed in a plan before any model code existed. Its sha256 was recorded on the wiki page at the time given. The plan is internal; its rules are restated in this artifact's inputs.

relationship_to_earlier_forecasts: Additive. Block 11 and every Kenya forecast stay frozen and are scored as registered. This forecast imports the 9 October Kenya model unchanged.

rules.ambiguity: Anything else unclear is decided by a reviewer other than the author, citing the authority statement, and recorded as an attribution in data/international-events.json.
rules.authorities: Nigeria's Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, NCDC, WHO (Disease Outbreak News, regional office, Director-General), Africa CDC, ECDC or US CDC. A press report alone does not count; a state broadcaster or national news agency carrying a minister's or NCDC official's statement does.
rules.registration_timing: Only reports first published after the registration entry count. If a qualifying report was published between 2026-10-20 22:45 UTC and that entry, the question is void.
rules.void: Void if, by 2026-11-20, an authority states that the first case is not a case of this outbreak, for example a different ebolavirus species or a discarded result.
rules.void_status_note: WHO's Regional Office for Africa stated on 20 October that a laboratory test confirmed Bundibugyo virus, which effectively settles the species condition; the rule is kept as registered.
rules.what_counts: Any further confirmed case in Nigeria counts unless an authority reports a stay, in the 21 days before onset, in an area with a confirmed case in the 42 days before that onset (a new importation). A contact of the first case counts, and so does a case of unknown source acquired in Nigeria.
rules.where_the_case_falls_ill: A case confirmed in another country after travel from Nigeria counts only if the authority states it was infected in Nigeria.

scoring_plan.scored_by: Brier score at a coverage review naming its sources, made between 2026-11-21 and 2026-12-05. Silence never resolves NO.

scoring_plan.wording: The result is reported as a probability beside the outcome and is never called a hit or a miss. One outcome cannot separate this forecast from the benchmarks, and the result says nothing about Nigeria's response.

validation.note: Negative mean_brier_difference favours the calibrated model; a difference smaller than twice its standard error is not evidence of a better forecaster. The episode features were coded by people who knew the outcomes, so even the leave-one-out scores are optimistic.
